title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: U.S. markets are closed today for Thanksgiving (half day Friday); Wednesday's wild session ended with the S&P 500 down 0.3% and Nasdaq down 0.6% after an intraday plunge of more than 4%, while the Dow rose 0.3%.
Markets: S&P Global put Nvidia on credit watch for a possible downgrade of its AA rating, citing board/governance vulnerabilities; shares fell 3.9% Wednesday.
Markets: Short-seller Michael Burry closed out his Nasdaq-100 put position, saying he's now 'temporarily almost entirely long.'
Companies: Nvidia boardroom turmoil keeps rippling through AI-linked stocks even after Jensen Huang resumed the CEO role this week.
Companies: Thanksgiving gas prices averaged $3.59/gallon, narrowly missing the 2022 record after falling about 70 cents over the past month on easing Mideast supply fears.

Macro/Policy: The Trump administration proposed fresh tariffs on China, Vietnam, the EU and dozens of other countries over subsidies, including 20% on most Chinese goods (up to 40% if talks collapse).

Macro/Policy: Axios scoop - AI executives are splitting over Anthropic's view that humanity should eventually cede decisions to superintelligent AI, with Meta's Alexandr Wang and OpenAI's Sam Altman pushing back on Dario Amodei's stance.
Macro/Policy: House GOP plans to bring the bipartisan, Senate-passed permitting/transmission bill to the floor next week; TD Cowen puts a 75% chance on it becoming law this year.
